# Spec — writing `spec.md` the organization's way

You are writing `projects/<PRJ>/intents/<NN-slug>/spec.md`. Below is what the organization's lifecycle says about this step, the sections the
artifact must carry, and its template. The lifecycle policy is the authority; this is a copy of it.

## What the lifecycle says — Spec

Template: `policies/reference/lifecycles/ai-sdlc/spec.md`

The spec says what will be true and how it is designed. Its open questions are ruled one at a time, by the
person who approves the spec, before it is approved.

## What `spec.md` must carry

Open with the template's front matter and the Status line `**Status:** DRAFT`. You never write APPROVED: gov
writes it when a person approves the change request and it merges.

Then every one of these sections, as a `##` heading, in this order:

- Scope recap
- Design
- Current state (file:line)
- Acceptance criteria
- Contradictions and open Q's
- Dependencies, risks, test strategy

## The template — `policies/reference/lifecycles/ai-sdlc/spec.md`

````markdown
---
domain: development
layer: spec
owner: <owner>
compliance: C01
status: draft
---

# Spec <NN>: <title>

**Status:** DRAFT
<!-- One of: DRAFT · APPROVED by <who> <date> (<change request link>) · STALE (<why>).
     gov writes the APPROVED line when the change request is approved by a person and merged; never write it by hand. -->

Intent: [intent.md](intent.md)

## Scope recap
| # | Deliverable | Comes from |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | <what will be true> | <intent line / ruling> |

## Design
<How it works. Draw a flow, sequence or state diagram as Mermaid text where it has one.>

## Current state (file:line)
<What exists today, with file:line evidence.>

## Acceptance criteria
| Part | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|
| D1 | <checkable statement> |

## Contradictions and open Q's
<!-- Each question numbered, with options and a recommendation; ruled one at a time before approval. -->
**Q1 — <title>.** (a) … · (b) … **Recommend (a)** — <why>.

## Dependencies, risks, test strategy
<What this needs first; what could go wrong and the mitigation; how it is tested.>
````
